narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and unfortunately, we were unable to approve it at this time. Based on the information provided, the system predicted a 58% likelihood that the loan could pose a higher risk of repayment difficulties. While this doesn’t mean you’ll definitely struggle to repay, it does suggest that certain aspects of your financial situation raised concerns compared to others who were approved.

The most significant factor in this decision was the current balance in your checking account. Unlike most approved applicants—half of whom have at least some funds available—your account shows a negative balance. This was the strongest signal that influenced the outcome, as it may indicate limited financial flexibility to handle additional debt. The length of the loan you requested also played a key role. At 42 months, it’s more than twice as long as the average approved loan (19 months), which increases the time during which unexpected financial challenges could arise.

On the other hand, your credit history worked slightly in your favor. While it’s noted as "critical" due to past or existing credits, this wasn’t as severe as other riskier patterns, like repeated payment delays. Still, this positive aspect wasn’t enough to outweigh the concerns about your account balance and loan duration.

Other details, like the purpose of the loan (repairs) and your savings (less than 100 DM), also factored into the decision. Repairs are less common among approved applicants, and most have at least some savings as a financial cushion. Additionally, being unemployed—while not the main driver—further contributed to the assessment, as steady income is important for managing loan payments.

To improve your chances in the future, focusing on stabilizing your checking account balance and reducing the requested loan term could make a meaningful difference. Building even a small savings buffer and exploring shorter repayment periods might also help. If your financial situation changes—such as securing employment or improving your account status—you’re welcome to reapply later. We understand this isn’t the outcome you hoped for, but we want to ensure any loan we approve is manageable for you in the long run.
